findings.issue: fetchJson caches every result — including nulls from !response.ok and caught errors — forever in a globalThis promise map, so a transient API failure permanently poisons the home catalogue or any resource page until process restart
findings.suggestion: Only cache successful responses; on failure remove the promise from the map (retry-in-flight semantics) and surface transient errors differently from genuine 404s

findings.issue: All fetch errors are swallowed to null, so an API outage renders 'Not found' pages instead of an error state
findings.suggestion: Let non-404 errors reject (or return a tagged error) and render a server error page; reserve null for real 404s

findings.issue: In-memory cache keyed by raw user-supplied URLs (/pokemon/<anything>) with no eviction — unbounded memory growth under URL fuzzing
findings.suggestion: Only cache known-resource URLs (ids from the species index), or add an LRU bound; never cache misses keyed by user input

findings.issue: Game select navigates with window.location.assign, forcing a full document reload and defeating Qwik's SPA navigation and resumability
findings.suggestion: Use useNavigate() to set the path with the ?game= query param; keep the #moves hash

findings.issue: The routeLoader returns the full 1,025-entry catalogue, so it is serialized into every home HTML response and re-fetched from the server on every pagination SPA navigation
findings.suggestion: Acceptable for the first paint, but consider a lighter loader for query-only SPA navigations or paginated server filtering with client-side search on the current page's data

findings.issue: Client components import humanize/displayDex from the same module that holds server-only fetch code and the globalThis store (data.ts:48-50 side effects execute in the browser)
findings.suggestion: Split pure formatters (humanize, displayDex, formatValue, latestEnglishFlavor) into a client-safe module; keep fetchJson and the store in a server-only module

findings.issue: API records are typed `any` throughout, so typos like flavor_text_entries fail silently at runtime
findings.suggestion: Define minimal interfaces for the handful of PokeAPI records actually consumed; strict mode is on, so this is cheap

findings.issue: Not-found routes respond with HTTP 200; framework supports fail(404) in routeLoader$ or the qwik-city not-found flow
findings.suggestion: Throw a 404 error from the loaders when the resource is missing so the server responds with a real status code

findings.issue: Cold start fetches ~1,075 URLs (1025 pokemon records + generations + types) before the first home response, a multi-second first-byte latency
findings.suggestion: Reduce per-entry pokemon fetches to just type/sprite needs, or warm the cache at server start instead of on first request

findings.issue: Three different URL-mutation mechanisms across the app (window.history.replaceState here, window.location.assign on the pokemon page, plain <a> links elsewhere)
findings.suggestion: Standardise on useNavigate()/Link; keep raw history.replaceState only where the router genuinely can't do it, with a comment saying why

summary: A well-organised, current-version Qwik City app that uses routeLoader$, signals and DocumentHead the way the docs recommend, with clean readable routes that map one-to-one to the spec. The merge blockers are in the data layer: swallowed fetch errors that are cached forever, an unbounded user-keyed cache, and a server/client module boundary leak. One round of review changes — cache/error fixes, a data-module split, and useNavigate for the game picker — gets this to approvable.
